summary: Frontend-only verification of the new hover-cursor affordances on /demo-trade drawings. All primary acceptance criteria pass. Two separate Playwright runs against the live VPS (https://api.binaryfundglobal.com) with JWT injected into localStorage.bfg_token. Cursor was read from the chart host element (parent of [data-testid='drawing-canvas']) via inline style.cursor and getComputedStyle.
verified_behaviours: Rectangle corner handles (TL & BR — the only 2 stored corners) hover -> 'nwse-resize'. This is correct because a Rectangle drawing stores 2 points on the NW-SE diagonal; both handles are on that diagonal so both are nwse-resize. There is no TR/BL handle to produce nesw-resize for rectangles.

Trend_line: body -> 'move', both endpoints -> 'nwse-resize' (endpoints drawn on NW-SE diagonal). Code path in cursorFor() correctly falls through to dx*dy sign, and abs<4 branches produce ns/ew when endpoints are nearly aligned.
Empty chart space hover -> cursor resets to '' (computed 'auto').
While a tool is armed (mode='draw') the host cursor is 'crosshair'.
While dragging the body of a selected shape the cursor is 'grabbing'; after pointerup it resets to '' immediately.

60-move sweep across chart with drawings: 0 longtasks >50ms observed via PerformanceObserver, no console errors, no visible jank. crosshair-vert / crosshair-horz elements still present (tracked by TradeChart's own DOM crosshair which is unrelated to host.style.cursor).

Regression - interior click selects the drawing (drawing-style-bar appears), draw-copy-selected button is present and clickable, click on empty space deselects (style bar unmounts) and returns pan cursor.
action_items: OPTIONAL / not in scope of iter 46: There is no keyboard/UI-affordance to disarm the currently-active drawing tool without completing a shape. Escape does nothing; clicking the already-active [data-testid="draw-tool-<id>"] does not toggle draw mode off. Consider wiring Escape (or a second click on the active tool) to reset mode back to 'idle' — during automated testing this made re-hovering after arming difficult.

OPTIONAL: For rectangles, if TradingView-parity is desired, the model could expose 4 corner handles (TL, TR, BR, BL) so TR/BL show nesw-resize. Current 2-handle model is functional but limits diagonal resize direction options.
critical_code_review_comments: DrawingLayer.jsx cursorFor() logic is correct and cheap (pure hit-test math, no allocations).
Hover handler is properly rAF-throttled and registered as passive pointermove on host; pointerleave clears the cursor. Good.
onDown sets 'grabbing' for body hits and the matching resize cursor for handle hits; onUp resets host.style.cursor = ''. Symmetric and clean.
onHover early-returns if target closest [data-chart-overlay] — correctly avoids running hit-tests while hovering the style bar / drawings panel.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Cursor is set on the chart HOST element = parentElement of [data-testid='drawing-canvas'] (NOT the canvas itself, because the canvas has pointer-events:none outside draw mode). Read via host.style.cursor (inline) or getComputedStyle(host).cursor. Rectangles have only 2 handles (both on NW-SE diagonal -> nwse-resize). To disarm draw mode reliably in tests, either draw a 2-point shape (mode auto-exits) or pick a different tool — do NOT rely on Escape or on toggling the same tool button.
